extracted.intended_audience: applicants and practitioners filing utility and plant patent applications (patent attorneys, agents, and pro se applicants)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing and correcting drawings in new utility and plant patent applications so the Office of Patent Application Processing (OPAP) can effectively scan and reproduce them for publication. Covers acceptability standards, common defects, filing requirements for corrected drawings, and related procedural consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: OPAP review purpose and scope
rubrics_metrics.description: OPAP performs an initial review of drawings in new utility and plant patent applications to determine whether the drawings can be effectively scanned for publication purposes. Design applications are not published and OPAP does not review design patent drawings for publication purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The standard of review is such that most drawings, including those indicated by applicant to be 'informal drawings,' will be acceptable. OPAP inspects whether drawings can be effectively scanned and adequately reproduced; if not acceptable, OPAP will object and notify applicant to submit acceptable drawings within a set time period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Line quality and legibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Lines and letters must be heavy enough to permit adequate reproduction; text (reference characters, sheet numbers, view numbers) must be plain and legible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OPAP may object if line quality is too light or text is illegible. See 37 CFR 1.84(l) and (p)(1). Remedy by submitting corrected drawings with sufficiently dark/heavy lines and clearly printed reference labels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presence of lead lines
rubrics_metrics.description: Drawings must include lead lines — lines between reference characters and the details referred to.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OPAP will object if lead lines are missing. See 37 CFR 1.84(q). Ensure every reference numeral has a visible lead line pointing to the claimed feature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excessive or non-English text
rubrics_metrics.description: Drawings must not contain excessive text and text must be in English.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OPAP may object if there is excessive text or text not in English (for example, a flow chart originally not in English that has been marked up to include English text). See 37 CFR 1.84(o), 1.84(p)(2), and 37 CFR 1.52(d). Convert text to concise English labels or move explanatory text to the specification where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Margins and sheet size
rubrics_metrics.description: Each sheet must have appropriate margins and be on approved paper sizes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required margins: top at least 2.5 cm (1 inch), left at least 2.5 cm (1 inch), right at least 1.5 cm (5/8 inch), bottom at least 1.0 cm (3/8 inch). Acceptable sheet sizes: 21.0 cm x 29.7 cm (A4) or 21.6 cm x 27.9 cm (8-1/2 x 11 inches). See 37 CFR 1.84(f) and (g). OPAP will object if margins or paper size are incorrect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figure numbering and labeling
rubrics_metrics.description: If there is more than one figure, each figure must be labeled 'Fig.' with a consecutive Arabic numeral (1, 2, etc.) or an Arabic numeral and capital letter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OPAP will object when multiple figures are not properly labeled. See 37 CFR 1.84(u)(1). Use consistent, consecutive 'Fig.' labels on every figure sheet.

rubrics_metrics.name: Photographs that could be illustrated by drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: Photographs of the claimed invention that are capable of illustration by other means, such as ink drawings, should not be used if they are illegible after scanning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OPAP may object to photographs that could be replaced by line drawings and which are illegible after scanning. See 37 CFR 1.84(b). Where possible, supply clear line drawings instead of photographs or supply higher-quality images that scan legibly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Color drawings and photographs
rubrics_metrics.description: Color drawings or color photographs require a petition to accept color drawings/photographs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OPAP will object to color drawings/photographs filed without a petition. Note: the requirement for submitting a black-and-white photocopy of any color drawings/photographs has been eliminated. Follow petition procedures when color is essential and justified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement and procedure for submitting corrected drawings after objection
rubrics_metrics.description: If OPAP objects and issues a Notice requiring corrected drawings within a set time period (usually two months), corrected drawings must be filed in paper to the mailing address set forth in the Notice, along with any other items required by OPAP.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to timely file corrected drawings as required by the Notice can lead to abandonment of the application. No fee is necessary for filing corrected drawings required by OPAP. Comply with the Notice's instructions (format, accompanying items, mailing address) to avoid abandonment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication reflects filing quality unless better drawings are voluntarily submitted
rubrics_metrics.description: In most situations, patent application publications and patents will reflect the quality of the drawings that are included with a patent application on filing unless applicant voluntarily submits better quality drawings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants who wish publication to show higher-quality drawings should voluntarily submit improved drawings as set forth in MPEP § 1121. Otherwise, published documents will reproduce the drawings as filed.
